s: This unit records Confucius's teachings on shame, virtue, learning, government, loyalty, justice, and the conduct of the superior man. It discusses historical figures including Kwan Chung, the duke Hwan, Tsze-lu, and others in relation to virtue, political service, and propriety. Confucius says that perfect virtue is difficult, that injury should be repaid with justice, and that kindness should be repaid with kindness. He also describes the superior man as self-cultivating, modest in speech, diligent in action, and concerned with giving rest to others.

s: Confucius teaches that thinking only of salary under either good or bad government is shameful, and that a scholar who loves comfort is not fit to be a scholar. He praises virtue, justice, modest speech, self-cultivation, and loyalty guided by instruction, while criticizing obstinacy, covetousness, and conduct without principle. He describes the superior man as cultivating himself to give rest to others and all the people.

l: The Analects of Confucius, Book XVI (Ke She), The Analects of Confucius, Book XVI (Ke She), The Analects, Book XVI: Ke She / CHAP. I. 1. The head of the Chi family was going to attack
s: The head of the Chi family plans to attack Chwan-yu, and Zan Yu and Chi-lu report this to Confucius. Confucius says Zan Yu is at fault for assisting the plan and argues that Chwan-yu has a legitimate place within the State. He teaches that rulers should seek harmony, contented repose, and the proper ordering of their people rather than fear scarcity. Confucius concludes that the Chi family’s internal divisions and hostile movements may bring sorrow within its own court.

s: Confucius condemns the planned attack on Chwan-yu and says that Zan Yu is at fault for supporting it. He teaches that rulers should maintain harmony, contented repose, and the proper places of their people, attracting remoter people through civil culture and virtue.

s: Rulers and chiefs should be concerned that people keep their several places and enjoy contented repose. When harmony prevails, there will be no scarcity of people, and when contented repose exists, there will be no rebellious upsettings.

l: civil culture and virtue, The Analects of Confucius, Book XVI (Ke She), The Analects, Book XVI: Ke She / CHAP. I. 1. The head of the Chi family was going to attack

l: The Analects of Confucius, Book XVI (Ke She), The Analects of Confucius, Book XVI (Ke She), CHAP. II. 1. Confucius said, 'When good government prevails
s: Confucius explains how authority over ceremonies, music, and punitive military expeditions reflects the quality of government in the empire. Under good government, these powers proceed from the son of Heaven; under bad government, they proceed from the princes and increasingly lower officials. He states that when right principles prevail in the kingdom, government will not be in the hands of the Great officers and the common people will not engage in discussions.

l: Confucius, The Analects of Confucius, Book XVI (Ke She), CHAP. II. 1. Confucius said, 'When good government prevails

s: Confucius explains that men find enjoyment in three things that are advantageous and three things that are injurious.
